job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
• Lead financial performance
  • Drive continuous improvement
  • Partner with the business
Are you a commercially minded finance leader who combines strong technical expertise with a strategic approach to financial management?
 
Johnson Winter Slattery is seeking an experienced Financial Controller to lead the finance function, strengthen financial governance and provide meaningful commercial insights to support business performance and decision-making.
 
Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this is a key leadership role with responsibility for financial and management reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, compliance and the development of a high-performing finance team. You will work closely with senior leadership and stakeholders across the firm, ensuring the finance function delivers accurate, timely and actionable information while continually improving systems, processes and controls.
 
About the role
As Financial Controller, you will provide strategic and operational leadership across the finance function, ensuring financial integrity, effective controls and compliance with all relevant statutory and regulatory obligations.
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Financial leadership and reporting: Oversee the delivery of accurate and timely financial reporting, management accounting and financial analysis to support informed decision-making.
  • Budgeting and forecasting: Lead annual budgets, financial forecasts and performance monitoring, providing insights into financial results, risks and opportunities.
  • Cash flow management: Oversee cash flow, liquidity planning and financial performance against budgets and key performance indicators.
  • Governance and compliance: Ensure compliance with Australian accounting standards, taxation requirements and statutory obligations, including GST, FBT, payroll tax and superannuation.
  • Trust accounting: Oversee trust accounting processes and ensure compliance with applicable legislation, regulations and professional standards.
  • Team leadership: Lead, mentor and develop a multidisciplinary finance team, fostering accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Systems and process improvement: Identify and implement improvements to financial systems, reporting frameworks, internal controls and operational efficiency.
  • Business partnering: Work collaboratively with the COO, senior leaders and operational stakeholders to provide commercial advice, explain financial performance and support business objectives.
  • Audit and stakeholder management: Coordinate external audits and maintain effective relationships with auditors, accountants and other relevant stakeholders.
About you
You are an experienced finance professional with the credibility, judgement and leadership capability to manage a complex finance function and influence outcomes across the business.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • CA/CPA qualified with a degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce or a related discipline.
  • 10+ years' experience in senior finance roles, with responsibility for financial management, reporting and compliance.
  • Demonstrated success leading, mentoring and developing finance teams.
  • Strong knowledge of Australian accounting standards, taxation requirements and financial governance.
  • Advanced capabilities in financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting and reporting.
  • Excellent commercial acumen, analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to build trusted relationships and communicate complex financial information to non-financial stakeholders.
  • A proactive approach to process improvement, systems optimisation and strengthening internal controls.
  • Strong ethical standards, integrity, and professionalism.
  • Experience in a legal or professional services environment will be highly regarded.
 
Why join Johnson Winter Slattery?
This is an opportunity to take ownership of a critical business function and make a tangible contribution to the firm's financial performance and long-term objectives.

You will have the opportunity to partner with senior leadership, influence business decisions, lead an established finance team and drive improvements that enhance financial insight, operational efficiency and governance.

If you are a commercially focused finance leader who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on financial management, we would welcome your application.
 
Apply now
If you're interested in this opportunity, apply now including your CV and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience and suitability for the role. For a confidential discussion, contact Phil Scardigno at a&co Recruitment Partners on 0439 074 202 or email phil.scardigno@aandco.au

job.title: Payroll Officer
job.description:
Part-Time | Fixed-Term Maternity Leave Cover | 3 Days per Week

Bring your payroll expertise to a role that makes a difference.
Are you an experienced Payroll Officer who loves getting the details right, takes pride in delivering an exceptional service, and wants your work to contribute to something meaningful?

Lifeline WA is seeking a capable, proactive and people-focused Payroll Officer to join our team on a fixed-term maternity leave contract. This is an opportunity to take ownership of end-to-end payroll in a purpose-driven organisation, supporting the people who help make a difference in the lives of others.

Working three full days per week, you'll play an important role in ensuring our people are paid accurately and on time, while maintaining strong payroll controls, compliance and records. You'll be part of a collaborative team that values trust, respect, connection and excellence.

The opportunity
  • Start date: Ideally 4 January 2027
  • Contract: Fixed-term maternity leave cover through to 30 June 2028
  • Working days: Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday — all three days are essential.
What you'll be doing You'll coordinate accurate, timely and compliant fortnightly payroll for approximately 170 employees, including around 70 full-time staff and 100 Crisis Supporters who are paid based on timesheets.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing the end-to-end fortnightly payroll cycle, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time.
  • Maintaining employee payroll records, including new starters, contract changes, pay point progressions, allowances, deductions, leave and terminations.
  • Applying your knowledge of the SCHADS Award to support accurate pay calculations and compliant payroll outcomes.
  • Administering payroll systems, investigating discrepancies and resolving payroll exceptions.
  • Completing payroll journals, payments, statutory lodgements, reporting and reconciliations.
  • Managing month-end payroll processes and associated balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Maintaining complete payroll documentation, audit trails and strong internal controls.
  • Responding to employee and manager enquiries with professionalism, discretion and a service-focused approach.
Ideally, you'll bring:
  • At least three years' experience in end-to-end payroll processing.
  • Strong working knowledge of the SCHADS Award and relevant payroll compliance requirements will be highly regarded.
  • Experience managing fortnightly payroll for a diverse workforce, including timesheet-based employees.
  • Experience with ELMO and confidence navigating payroll and HR systems.
  • Practical experience with payroll reconciliations, journals, lodgements, reporting and month-end processes.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate and resolve payroll discrepancies.
  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities within tight deadlines.
  • Above all, you'll bring a positive attitude, a proactive mindset and a genuine commitment to being part of a supportive, values-driven team.

Interviews are expected to commence in the next few weeks so please apply today!

If you’re interested in this opportunity, please get in touch with Karen McGlynn on 0406 833 625 or email karen.mcglynn@aandco.au with your updated resume.

You'll be responsible for fostering constructive workplace relationships, managing industrial risk, supporting enterprise bargaining activities, and ensuring compliance with employment legislation and industrial instruments. 

Key responsibilities include:
  • Providing expert advice on industrial and employee relations matters
  • Leading enterprise bargaining strategy and negotiations
  • Building and maintaining effective relationships with unions and key stakeholders
  • Managing industrial disputes, grievance matters and Fair Work Commission proceedings
  • Advising on enterprise agreement interpretation and application
  • Supporting compliance reviews, audits and industrial relations projects
  • Developing policies, procedures and strategies that strengthen workplace relations outcomes
  • Coaching leaders and HR professionals to build organisational IR capability. 
About You To be successful, you'll bring:
  • Significant experience in Industrial Relations, Employee Relations, HR Business Partnering or a related specialist role

  • Experience working within complex and unionised environments
  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise bargaining activities and industrial negotiations
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills
  • Experience managing complex workplace investigations, disputes and case management

  • A collaborative People & Culture team environment

If you're a confident IR professional who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with practical problem-solving, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Director, Policy & Operations
job.description:
ACOSH (Australian Council on Smoking and Health) is Australia's leading tobacco control advocacy organisation, with a proud history spanning more than 50 years. Working with governments, health organisations and communities across the country, ACOSH advocates for the end of tobacco and nicotine addiction in Australia and drives policy and regulatory reform that delivers meaningful public health outcomes.

We are seeking an experienced and influential leader to join ACOSH as Director, Policy & Operations. This is a pivotal leadership role that combines strategic planning, stakeholder engagement, organisational leadership and operational oversight, helping ensure ACOSH continues to deliver impact at both a state and national level.

About the Role
Reporting directly to the CEO, this role will play a key part in supporting the organisation's strategic direction and ongoing growth. This is a broad leadership role that requires someone who is comfortable operating at both a strategic and operational level. You'll help shape policy positions, oversee key organisational initiatives, contribute to financial planning and ensure the organisation is well positioned to respond to emerging challenges and opportunities.

Success in the role will require strong stakeholder management skills, excellent judgement and the ability to navigate complex environments. You'll work closely with the CEO, Board, member organisations and external partners to drive outcomes that align with ACOSH's mission and strategic priorities.

About You
You're an accomplished leader with strong commercial and financial acumen who enjoys bringing people together to achieve common goals.

You are a strategic thinker who can see the bigger picture while maintaining a strong focus on execution. You communicate with confidence, build trusted relationships and know how to influence outcomes across a diverse stakeholder group.

You will likely bring:
  • Experience operating in a senior leadership role
  • Strong financial and commercial capability
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills
  • Proven stakeholder management and relationship-building experience
  • The ability to develop strategy and translate it into practical outcomes
  • Experience leading projects, initiatives or organisational change
  • A collaborative and values-driven leadership style
Experience within public policy, advocacy, government, health, not-for-profit or member based organisations will be highly regarded.

Why Join ACOSH?
ACOSH is a respected and influential organisation with a clear mission and a long history of creating positive change. As Australia's leading tobacco control advocacy body, the organisation continues to play a critical role in shaping policy and protecting the health of Australians.

You'll join a passionate and purpose driven team where your work will have genuine impact. This is an opportunity to contribute to important public health outcomes while helping shape the future direction of a highly regarded organisation.

What's in it for You?
This is a rare opportunity to join the executive leadership team of an organisation that influences policy and drives meaningful change across Australia.

You'll have the opportunity to work alongside respected leaders, engage with senior decision makers and play a key role in advancing ACOSH's mission. The role offers variety, autonomy and the chance to make a lasting contribution to an important cause.
